Sacred Valley of the Incas: Pisac and Ollantaytambo

Duration: full day. Price: USD 220 per person.

A trip through the Sacred Valley of the Incas takes you into the Andean countryside to discover traditional crafts and the heritage of one of South America’s greatest civilisations.

The tour includes:

Pisac: Visit the local craft market for ceramics, wool products, silverwork, leather goods and traditional souvenirs.

Awanakancha: See llamas, alpacas, guanacos and vicuñas up close, and learn how wool is traditionally processed and dyed using natural materials.

Ollantaytambo: Explore one of the most important Inca archaeological sites. Its monumental terraces, stone buildings and surviving fortifications give you a sense of the scale and power of the Inca Empire.

Enjoy a buffet lunch at a restaurant serving Peruvian cuisine.

Return to Cusco. Overnight at the 4-star Xima Cusco or a hotel of the same category.

Vinicunca (Rainbow Mountain)

Duration: full day. Group tour with an English-speaking guide: USD 55 per person. Private tour with an English-speaking guide for groups of 2 or more: USD 200 per person.

Known around the world as Rainbow Mountain, Vinicunca is one of Peru’s most unusual natural wonders. Its slopes are streaked with mineral layers that formed over millions of years. Reds, yellows, greens, whites and other colours form bands against the Andean peaks.

Vinicunca is about 100 kilometres from Cusco, in Quispicanchi Province, at an elevation of around 5,200 metres. From here you can see the surrounding mountain ranges and Ausangate, a mountain sacred to the Incas.

The tour starts at around 04:00 and returns to Cusco at approximately 19:00. Breakfast and lunch are included.

The route is at high altitude and requires good physical stamina. You can ride a horse for part of the ascent if you wish. Horse hire costs USD 40.

Overnight at the 4-star Xima Cusco or a hotel of the same category.
